_doc: WS-6a latency SLO, enforced post-deploy by scripts/deploy_api.sh. Tighter than the nightly alerting bands in served_probe_thresholds.json, and for a different purpose: this runs immediately after a known deploy against a machine Fly has already health-checked, so it is a regression gate rather than a drift detector. Anchors measured 2026-09-05: health warm 31.9-45.3 ms, search server-side total_ms 506.5-617.7. Bounds sit at roughly 10x and 2.5x those, tight enough that a real regression fails the release and loose enough that provider and network variance does not.
_cold_start: Deliberately not gated. fly.toml sets grace_period = 5m on the health check, so a boot slower than that flaps the machine into a restart and the deploy fails on its own -- the cold-start bound exists and Fly enforces it. An earlier version of this note claimed the machine would already have answered /api/health by the time the gate runs, so every number it saw would be warm. That is false: min_machines_running = 0 and auto_stop_machines = suspend leave the app stopped after a deploy, and the probe's own first request is what resumes it. Measured 2026-09-09: 502 on the first call and 34.9 s on the second, which failed this gate on a boot. scripts/deploy_api.sh now polls /api/health until it answers before measuring. max_health_cold_ms stays generous and records the resume path, measured at 10762-47217 ms.
